summary: Validated iteration adding PARTIAL PAYMENTS to the 40% unlock paywall (min 500 EUR per abono, accumulating to 2,660 EUR). 14 backend pytest cases + full Playwright E2E. ALL 21 declared scenarios pass green: status payload exposes min_partial_eur/total_paid_eur/remaining_eur, start seeds payments=[], proof endpoint enforces min/max/duplicate-hash/short-hash/zero/negative validations, accumulates payments, transitions pending_payment→in_review at exact closure with FIFO priority_rank, defaults to remaining when amount_eur omitted, returns 404 after in_review. Admin queue still lists in_review records (now with payments[]) and admin approve mirrors flag onto user. Frontend renders panel correctly in fresh, partial (19%, 56%) states, modal pre-loads remaining, quick-pick chips render (€500/€1.000/Total restante), submit copy switches between 'Registrar abono' and 'Completar y enviar a revisión', tx_hash links to Tronscan, withdraw-unlock-indicator regression OK.
critical_code_review_comments: partial_unlock.py:228 has correct floating-point tolerance (`amount + 0.01 < remaining`) so the LAST payment is allowed to be < MIN_PARTIAL_EUR when it just closes the gap — important UX for residuals.
Duplicate-hash check is case-insensitive (.lower()) and scoped to the same unlock — exactly right.
Status payload returns `total_paid_eur` and `remaining_eur` even when `active_request` is None (defaults to 0 / 2660), which keeps the frontend payload-shape consistent.
PartialUnlockPanel.jsx:577 quick-pick chip filter elegantly hides the €500 / €1.000 chips when remaining is below them but always keeps the 'Total restante' chip — good UX.
Submit-button copy logic at line 620 (`Number(partialAmount) >= remaining - 0.01 && remaining > 0`) correctly handles the floating-point edge (e.g. 1160 vs 1160.00) for closure detection.

Minor (non-blocking) suggestion: `priority_rank` is incremented based on `count_documents({status:'in_review'})` BEFORE the update is written, so when two users complete simultaneously they could in theory both be assigned the same rank. For LIONSBIT volume this is a non-issue but a $inc-based atomic counter would be more defensive.

Minor (non-blocking): the `Mínimo por abono: €500 (o el monto exacto que cierra la activación)` toast copy is slightly more verbose than the backend's `Monto mínimo por abono parcial: 500 EUR`. Both are correct; just inconsistent. Frontend toast wins for clarity.
